messages.content: Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

**Senior Backend Engineer**
Remote (US) or Chicago office · $180–220k + equity

Roughly $4B a year in ACH and card settlement flows through us, on behalf of small-business lenders. Every one of those transactions crosses services this backend team owns.

Eleven engineers total. You'd sit in the payments core group — four of us who look after the ledger, the settlement engine, and the reconciliation jobs that fire at 2 a.m. and have to come out right.

**The work**

Go, mostly, with a Postgres ledger and Kafka between services. Your first quarter goes to the double-entry rewrite: a nine-year-old balance table has carried us well beyond what it was built for, and we're replacing it with no maintenance window. What comes after that is open, and worth arguing about.

On call runs one week in six. We cut paging volume by 60% last year instead of telling people to live with it, which is roughly how seriously we take it.

**Who we're after**

Five or more years on backend systems that hold state and cannot lose it. Actual SQL fluency, not ORM fluency. Somewhere in there you've debugged production at an hour you'd have preferred to be asleep, and then written the postmortem.

Fintech on your résumé helps but isn't required. Payments you can learn; judgment about correctness takes longer to build.

**How hiring goes**

Four conversations across two weeks — intro call, systems design discussion, a working session on real code from our repo, and time with the CTO. No take-home, no whiteboard algorithms.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
